# luminous_ui — Project Docs & Continuation System

This `docs/` tree is the **durable memory of the project**. It exists so any new
Claude Code session (or human) can resume work **without reloading the whole
codebase into context**. Read this file first, then load only the docs relevant
to your task.

> **These docs are a guide, not a rulebook.** They capture the current best plan
> and the *reasoning* behind it — not a fixed process to execute blindly. If,
> while working, the code or new context reveals a better or simpler approach,
> **propose it**: say what you'd change and why, and (once it's the direction)
> update the affected doc + record the shift in `decisions.md`. The plans exist
> to be improved, not obeyed. What must be preserved is the *rationale* and the
> *update trail*, so the next session understands why things are the way they are.

## New session? Resume protocol

1. Read **`progress.md`** — the single source of truth for *what's done, what's
   in flight, and where to pick up* (the **Resume point**).
2. Skim **`roadmap.md`** for the big picture (the five phases).
3. Open only the **`workstreams/<area>.md`** you're working on, plus any
   **`reference/`** file it points to. Do **not** read the other workstreams.
4. Follow **`conventions.md`** — especially the sub-agent policy and the
   end-of-session doc-update ritual.

## File map

| File | What it's for |
|---|---|
| `progress.md` | Living status + session log + the current **resume point**. Update every session. |
| `roadmap.md` | The phased plan (P1→P5) and dependencies. |
| `decisions.md` | Decision log (why we chose what) + locked assumptions. |
| `conventions.md` | How we work: sub-agents, doc ritual, code/test/commit rules. |
| `workstreams/backend-data.md` | **P1** — Bun+Hono API, tcgdex→D1 ingest, R2 images, auth, deck API, lobby DO. Contains the tcgdex API reference. |
| `workstreams/deck-builder.md` | **P2** — real cards in the builder, richer filters, editor + decks list. |
| `workstreams/simulator.md` | **P3** — the rules-driven game engine. |
| `workstreams/online.md` | **P4** — run the simulator over the lobby DO for real matches. |
| `workstreams/polish.md` | **P5** — profiles, avatars, lobby names, misc refinement. |
| `reference/ptcg-rules.md` | Condensed Pokémon TCG ruleset — the spec for the simulator (P3). |

## The one rule that keeps this working

**Keep context small.** Delegate research, code-mapping, and multi-file edits to
sub-agents (see `conventions.md`), load only the workstream you need, and write
what you learned back into these docs **before the session ends**.

2	
3	Five phases. Each has a detailed workstream doc; this is the map + dependencies.
4	Live status lives in `progress.md`, not here.
5	
6	## Phase 1 — Backend & Data Foundation → `workstreams/backend-data.md`
7	Stand up the Bun + Hono API on Cloudflare. Ingest real tcgdex card data into D1,
8	mirror images to R2, add accounts + auth (email/password + Discord/Google),
9	persist decks/folders, and stand up the lobby Durable Object (WebSocket) server.
10	**Unblocks everything else.**
11	
12	## Phase 2 — Deck Builder & Decks List (real cards) → `workstreams/deck-builder.md`
13	Replace the fixture card pool with the live catalog API. Complete the deck
14	editor (add/remove, counts, format validation, save/load) and the decks list
15	page (folders, CRUD, persistence). Upgrade filters using the richer tcgdex
16	fields (set/serie, rarity, HP, illustrator, regulation mark, ability/attack text,
17	energy cost).
18	*Depends on: P1 catalog + deck API.*
19	
20	## Phase 3 — Simulator Engine → `workstreams/simulator.md`
21	Research the official Pokémon TCG rules (`reference/ptcg-rules.md`) and build the
22	game engine: a deterministic state machine + a card-effect system driven by the
23	imported card data + descriptions. Iterative — accuracy improves pass over pass;
24	unimplemented cards degrade gracefully. The goal is to replicate the real game.
25	*Depends on: P2 (real, usable decks) + the ruleset.*
26	
27	## Phase 4 — Online Matches → `workstreams/online.md`
28	Run the P3 engine authoritatively inside the lobby Durable Object so two players
29	on different machines can play a real game. Swap the client lobby transport from
30	BroadcastChannel to WebSocket. Same engine as local play, with tweaks for
31	authority/hidden info.
32	*Depends on: P3 engine + P1 lobby DO.*
33	
34	## Phase 5 — Polish → `workstreams/polish.md`
35	Now that user + card data exist: player names & profile pictures on the lobby,
36	profiles, real deck-cover art, and general refinement. Threads through P2–P4 but
37	tracked separately so it isn't forgotten.
38	*Depends on: P1 user data.*

# Roadmap

Five phases. Each has a detailed workstream doc; this is the map + dependencies.
Live status lives in `progress.md`, not here.

## Phase 1 — Backend & Data Foundation → `workstreams/backend-data.md`
Stand up the Bun + Hono API on Cloudflare. Ingest real tcgdex card data into D1,
mirror images to R2, add accounts + auth (email/password + Discord/Google),
persist decks/folders, and stand up the lobby Durable Object (WebSocket) server.
**Unblocks everything else.**

## Phase 2 — Deck Builder & Decks List (real cards) → `workstreams/deck-builder.md`
Replace the fixture card pool with the live catalog API. Complete the deck
editor (add/remove, counts, format validation, save/load) and the decks list
page (folders, CRUD, persistence). Upgrade filters using the richer tcgdex
fields (set/serie, rarity, HP, illustrator, regulation mark, ability/attack text,
energy cost).
*Depends on: P1 catalog + deck API.*

## Phase 3 — Simulator Engine → `workstreams/simulator.md`
Research the official Pokémon TCG rules (`reference/ptcg-rules.md`) and build the
game engine: a deterministic state machine + a card-effect system driven by the
imported card data + descriptions. Iterative — accuracy improves pass over pass;
unimplemented cards degrade gracefully. The goal is to replicate the real game.
*Depends on: P2 (real, usable decks) + the ruleset.*

## Phase 4 — Online Matches → `workstreams/online.md`
Run the P3 engine authoritatively inside the lobby Durable Object so two players
on different machines can play a real game. Swap the client lobby transport from
BroadcastChannel to WebSocket. Same engine as local play, with tweaks for
authority/hidden info.
*Depends on: P3 engine + P1 lobby DO.*

## Phase 5 — Polish → `workstreams/polish.md`
Now that user + card data exist: player names & profile pictures on the lobby,
profiles, real deck-cover art, and general refinement. Threads through P2–P4 but
tracked separately so it isn't forgotten.
*Depends on: P1 user data.*

# Working Conventions

## Guidance, not gospel
These docs are a **living guide**, not a fixed process. You have context the
planning sessions didn't — the actual code, real data, what just broke. Use it:
- **Suggest better/different approaches** when you see them. Don't follow a task
  list off a cliff because it's written down.
- When you deviate: **explain the what + why**, prefer aligning with the user on
  anything significant, then **update the affected doc** and log the change in
  `decisions.md` (with its rationale). Small in-the-flow improvements don't need
  ceremony — just keep the docs honest.
- Locked assumptions and D-numbered decisions are **defaults with reasons**, not
  laws. Revisit any of them freely; the only hard rule is *don't reverse one
  silently* — leave a trail.
- Treat file/symbol references in these docs as **point-in-time** — verify against
  the current code before relying on them.

## Context hygiene (the point of this whole system)
- Load **`progress.md` + the one relevant `workstreams/*.md`** (+ its
  `reference/`). Don't read unrelated workstreams or sweep the repo.
- Prefer facts already written in these docs over re-deriving them.

## Sub-agent / workflow policy
Delegate to sub-agents to keep the main session's context lean:
- **Research** (rules, library docs, API behaviour) → a `general-purpose` agent
  that writes a condensed doc into `reference/` and returns only a summary.
- **Code mapping** ("how does X work today, what's missing") → an **Explore**
  agent (read-only; returns conclusions, not file dumps).
- **Implementation** of a self-contained slice → a `general-purpose` agent with
  a tight spec; it edits files and returns a summary + what to verify.
- **Review** before committing non-trivial work → `/code-review`.
- **Big fan-out** (e.g. authoring effect handlers for many cards, or a broad
  audit) → a **Workflow** (multi-agent). Note: user-triggered/opt-in — ask first.

Rule of thumb: if answering would mean reading many files, delegate it and keep
only the conclusion.

## Code & quality
- TypeScript strict; match the surrounding code's style and comment density.
- **Biome** for lint/format; **Vitest** for tests. Run **`bun run check`**
  (tsc + biome lint + vitest) before calling work done.
- Pure logic gets unit tests (see the many `*.test.ts` in the repo); DOM tests
  opt into jsdom per-file (`// @vitest-environment jsdom`).

## Git / commits
- Branch off `main` for non-trivial work; commit/push only when asked.
- Commit trailer per global config: `Co-Authored-By: Claude ...`.

## End-of-session ritual (do not skip)
1. Update `progress.md`: status table + session-log entry + **new resume point**.
2. Record any decision in `decisions.md`.
3. Write anything learned into the right workstream/reference doc so the next
   session doesn't rediscover it.

137:| D96 | Chien-Pao ex "Hail Blade" — the variable-count discard whose damage scales off it, and the engine's FIRST registry-authored attack (P3-M5, engine 0.47.0) | The resume point's first-named candidate and the damage family's hardest card. Chien-Pao ex **sv02-061** (Paldea Evolved, live SV pool — tcgdex-confirmed VERBATIM this session): "Hail Blade" ({W}{W}, "60×") = "You may discard **any amount** of {W} Energy from **your Pokémon**. This attack does 60 damage for each card you discarded in this way." **The D95 lesson held again:** the real print is broader than the backlog shorthand ("discard from this Pokémon") — it is "from **your** Pokémon" (the whole own board) and "for each **card**" (count-scaled). **Three gaps, closed together, in one coherent slice, reusing the most existing machinery: Model A (post-damage, §9.2 record-driven).** §8 applies damage BEFORE the effect program, so an attack whose number depends on a mid-attack choice cannot use the pre-W/R `AttackDamageBonus` fold (read off the board at declaration) — the honest model is base 0 + a program op that re-enters the W/R math AFTER the discard. (1) `discardEnergy` gained a **`from: "yours"`** arm — the CONTROLLER's whole board, the printed "your Pokémon", distinct from `yourActive`'s "this Pokémon"; the candidate scan (`attachedEnergies` whole-board) and apply (`discardEnergyApply` strips active+bench) already supported it, so it was `discardVictimSeat` + a from-arm, not new enumeration. (2) A **`count: "any"`** mode — the one DECLINABLE discard (0..all), a new `DiscardScope {kind:"upTo", max}` whose pick MAY be empty (every other discard scope is mandatory/exact), never collapsed by interchangeability (the COUNT is what the damage reads, so N identical {W} must offer N rows) and never forced (a real decision at every non-empty board). (3) A §9.2 **`recordAs`** on `discardEnergy` filing the discarded uids under a NEW `discarded` `EffectSlot` — "for each card you discarded **in this way**" is literally an op→op record read (the Miriam/Superior-Energy-Retrieval shape), so `discardEnergyApply` now returns `{state, discarded}` and `recordMoved` fires at every discard site (a no-op for the 5 pre-existing discard cards, which set no `recordAs`). The reader is a **new `damageDefender` op** `{per, count: EffectSlot}` that deals `per × recorded(slot).length` to the DEFENDER through the EXISTING **`snipeActive`** — the same full §8.5 pipeline Umbreon/Wo-Chien use to hit the Active (Weakness DOUBLES, Resistance/reduction subtract, the attacker's continuous pre-W/R bonus ADDS) — so it is genuine attack damage, NOT the flat put-counter model. **Because the program owns the damage, the printed "60×" base is SUPPRESSED** (attack.ts: a `programDamage` check — a program containing `damageDefender` drops the base + marks the "×" modifier simulated, exactly as the multiply family drops its own base; otherwise a 0-discard Hail Blade would deal 60 flat + double-count, and the "×" would flag `ATTACK_EFFECT_SKIPPED`). **The FIRST registry-authored attack** (the `programFor(id)?.attack` seam, unused until now): CHIEN_PAO's existing Shivery-Chill entry gained the `attack` program, because the variable-count sentence is one the deriver (`deriveAttackEffect` + the multiply/additive readers) deliberately refuses — so `deriveAttackEffect(verbatim)` STILL returns null and the providesEnergy/scaledDamage near-miss tests stay green. **A client change too** (no schema/API/DB): since M9 the web app runs on the real engine, so `GameHud.tsx`'s discard dialog gained the upTo/declinable branch (a capped multi-select, "Discard none"/"Discard N", always-ready Confirm). **HONESTY NOTE — landed under a hard autoloop landing without its own behavioural tests.** engineVersion 0.46.0 → **0.47.0**; `bun run typecheck` green and the **engine suite unchanged-green (929 tests)** — proving the implementation compiles and breaks nothing existing — but the dedicated `hailBlade.test.ts` (damage scaling / decline-is-0 / whole-board / Weakness / ex-KO prizes) was being written by a sub-agent STOPPED at the hard-landing before it produced the file, so those behaviours are code-reviewed-by-eye only. **The resume point makes writing them the immediate next slice, then `/code-review`.** *Why: the resume point named it first and as "its own session"; the code-map confirmed a three-gap slice, but each gap reused an existing seam (whole-board apply, the snipe W/R pipeline, the §9.2 record), so the honest whole-sentence implementation was tractable in one pass — the missing piece is verification, deferred (not skipped) with a loud resume point.* (2026-07-27) |

# Workstream: Simulator Engine (Phase 3)

Goal: replicate a real game of the Pokémon TCG well enough to play — first
approximately, then more accurately each pass. Reused by online matches (P4).

**Depends on:** P2 (real, usable decks) and `reference/ptcg-rules.md`.

## Approach
1. **Rules first.** `reference/ptcg-rules.md` (researched by a sub-agent) is the
   spec: setup, turn structure, zones, status conditions, KO/prizes, win
   conditions, first-turn restrictions, weakness/resistance math.
2. **Deterministic core.** A pure, seedable state machine:
   `GameState → Action → GameState` (+ emitted events for the UI/log). No
   randomness except a **seeded RNG** (shuffle, coin flips) so games are
   replayable and testable.
3. **Composable, data-driven card effects.** Most cards are minor variations on a
   few archetypes, so effects are authored as **data** — parameterized primitive
   ops over shared templates, not one function per card — and every op emits a
   semantic **event** the UI animates. Full design in the next section.
4. **State shape** builds on the existing playmat types
   (`src/features/playmat/types.ts`: BoardState, PlayerBoard, CardModel, zones)
   and the canonical `Card` (D5).

## Card-effect system — composable & data-driven

Most cards are minor variations on a **small set of effect archetypes**, so the
engine models effects as **composable primitives authored as data**, not a
bespoke function per card. Four layers:

1. **Primitive ops (`EffectOp`)** — the engine's instruction set: `Damage`,
   `ModifyDamage`, `PlaceDamageCounters`, `Heal`, `HealStatus`, `ApplyStatus`,
   `DrawCards`, `SearchDeck`, `Shuffle`, `AttachEnergy`, `DiscardEnergy`,
   `MoveCard`, `Switch`, `CoinFlip`, `ForEach`, `Conditional`, … Each op is a
   pure `(GameState, Ctx) → GameState` **and emits a semantic event** (below).
2. **Selectors & filters** — declarative targets (`self`, `opponentActive`,
   `yourBench`, `allYourPokemonMatching(filter)`, `playerChooses(filter)`) and
   card predicates (category / type / stage / isBasic / nameTag / energyCount…).
   Parameters, not code.
3. **Card effects as programs** — an attack is
   `{ cost, baseDamage, ops: EffectOp[] }`; an ability is
   `{ trigger, timing, oncePerTurn?, ops }`; a trainer / special energy is
   `{ provides?, ops }`. The whole effect is a small **data tree**.
4. **Archetype templates** — named builders for the common shapes, so a new card
   in a known family is one line of params:
   - `ballSearch({ cost, filter, dest })` → Nest / Great / Ultra / Quick / Level Ball
   - `handRefresh({ mode })` → Iono / Judge / Marnie / N
   - `gust()` → Boss's Orders-likes · `coinFlipDamage({ base, perHeads, flips })`
   - `energyAccelFromDiscard({ filter, target })`, …

### Grounded in real tcgdex data (fetched live)

249	export type EffectChoice =
250	  | { kind: "cards"; uids: string[] }
251	  | { kind: "pokemon"; ref: PokemonRef }

253	  /** The moveEnergy answer: up to `max` movable Energy uids (all sharing one
254	      source) moved onto `dest` — the compound decision validateChoice checks
255	      (same source, dest distinct from it). An empty `uids` is a decline. */
256	  | { kind: "moveEnergy"; uids: string[]; dest: PokemonRef }
257	  /** The discardEnergy answer: the Energy uids to discard — exactly `count` in
258	      total (`{kind:"total"}`) or exactly one per offered source Pokémon
259	      (`{kind:"each"}`), as validateChoice enforces. Never empty for those two
260	      MANDATORY scopes; the `{kind:"upTo"}` scope (Hail Blade's "any amount") is

265	      offered and appears once (one physical card cannot land on two Pokémon), and
266	      every `to` is an offered target, as validateChoice enforces. An empty list is
267	      a legal decline. */
268	  | { kind: "attachCards"; assignments: { uid: string; to: PokemonRef }[] }

274	/** What the ops ALREADY RUN in this program left behind for the ops still to
275	    come — each recording op's moved uids under its printed `EffectSlot` (§9.2:
276	    "in this way", "if you do", "with the effect of this card"). Threaded through
277	    a run as a mutable accumulator, exactly like `events`, and carried across a

280	    DELIBERATELY NOT A FIELD ON `EffectContext`, which the backlog named as the
281	    likely home. The context is WHO the program is running for — one seat, fixed

284	    that changes at nearly every op. Its sibling is `rest` ("the ops still to

Review target: `e035508~1..HEAD`

`xhigh effort → 5+5 angles × 8 candidates → 1-vote verify → sweep → ≤15 findings`

You are reviewing for **recall** at extra-high effort: catch every real bug. At
this level, catching real bugs matters more than avoiding false positives — a
missed bug ships. Err on the side of surfacing.

## Phase 0 — Gather the diff

Run `git diff @{upstream}...HEAD` (or `git diff main...HEAD` / `git diff HEAD~1`
if there's no upstream) to get the unified diff under review. If there are
uncommitted changes, or the range diff is empty, also run `git diff HEAD` and
include the working-tree changes in scope — the review often runs before the
commit. If a PR number, branch name, or file path was passed as an argument,
review that target instead. Treat this diff as the review scope.

## Phase 1 — Find candidates (5 correctness angles + 3 cleanup angles + 1 altitude angle + 1 conventions angle, up to 8 each)

Run **10 independent finder angles** via the Agent tool. Each
surfaces **up to 8 candidate findings**. Do NOT let one angle's conclusions
suppress another's — if two angles flag the same line for different reasons,
record both.

### Angle A — line-by-line diff scan

Read every hunk in the diff, line by line. Then Read the enclosing function for
each hunk — bugs in unchanged lines of a touched function are in scope (the PR
re-exposes or fails to fix them). For every line ask: what input, state, timing,
or platform makes this line wrong? Look for inverted/wrong conditions,
off-by-one, null/undefined deref, missing `await`, falsy-zero checks,
wrong-variable copy-paste, error swallowed in catch, unescaped regex metachars.

### Angle B — removed-behavior auditor

For every line the diff DELETES or replaces, name the invariant or behavior it
enforced, then search the new code for where that invariant is re-established.
If you can't find it, that's a candidate: a removed guard, a dropped error
path, a narrowed validation, a deleted test that was covering a real case.

### Angle C — cross-file tracer

For each function the diff changes, find its callers (Grep for the symbol) and
check whether the change breaks any call site: a new precondition, a changed
return shape, a new exception, a timing/ordering dependency. Also check callees:
does a parallel change in the same PR make a call unsafe?

### Angle D — language-pitfall specialist

Scan for the classic pitfalls of the diff's language/framework — for example:
JS falsy-zero, `==` coercion, closure-captured loop var; Python mutable default
args, late-binding closures; Go nil-map write, range-var capture; SQL injection;
timezone/DST drift; float equality. Flag any instance the diff introduces.

### Angle E — wrapper/proxy correctness

When the PR adds or modifies a type that wraps another (cache, proxy, decorator,
adapter): check that every method routes to the wrapped instance and not back
through a registry/session/global — e.g. a caching provider holding a
`delegate` field that resolves IDs via `session.get(...)` instead of
`delegate.get(...)` will re-enter the cache or recurse. Also check that the
wrapper forwards all the methods the callers actually use.

### Reuse

The angles above hunt for bugs; this one and the next two hunt for cleanup in
the changed code. Flag new code that re-implements something the codebase
already has — Grep shared/utility modules and files adjacent to the change,
and name the existing helper to call instead.

### Simplification

Flag unnecessary complexity the diff adds: redundant or derivable state,
copy-paste with slight variation, deep nesting, dead code left behind. Name
the simpler form that does the same job.

### Efficiency

Flag wasted work the diff introduces: redundant computation or repeated I/O,
independent operations run sequentially, blocking work added to startup or
hot paths. Also flag long-lived objects built from closures or captured
environments — they keep the entire enclosing scope alive for the object's
lifetime (a memory leak when that scope holds large values); prefer a
class/struct that copies only the fields it needs. Name the cheaper
alternative.

### Altitude

Check that each change is implemented at the right depth, not as a fragile
bandaid. Special cases layered on shared infrastructure are a sign the fix
isn't deep enough — prefer generalizing the underlying mechanism over adding
special cases.

### Conventions (CLAUDE.md)

Find the CLAUDE.md files that govern the changed code: the user-level
~/.claude/CLAUDE.md, the repo-root CLAUDE.md, plus any CLAUDE.md or
CLAUDE.local.md in a directory that is an ancestor of a changed file (a
directory's CLAUDE.md only applies to files at or below it). Read each one
that exists, then check the diff for clear violations of the rules they state.

Only flag a violation when you can quote the exact rule and the exact line
that breaks it — no style preferences, no vague "spirit of the doc"
inferences. In the finding, name the CLAUDE.md path and quote the rule so the
report can cite it. If no CLAUDE.md applies, return nothing for this angle.

Cleanup, altitude, and conventions candidates use the same
`file`/`line`/`summary` shape; in `failure_scenario`, state the concrete
cost (what is duplicated, wasted, harder to maintain, or which CLAUDE.md rule

summary:
Confirmed. `energyProvidesOf` derives from the card name via `/^(?:Basic )?(.+) Energy$/`: "Water Energy" → Water ({W}), while "fix-energy" doesn't match → Colorless (non-{W}). So test (b)'s "colorless not offered" exclusion is genuinely meaningful.

My review is complete. I traced all 8 tests against the CHIEN_PAO registry program (`packages/engine/src/registry.ts:273`), the deriver (`packages/engine/src/effects.ts:1324`), and the fixtures/deck (`packages/engine/src/testFixtures.ts:1471,1478,1486,2150`). All 8 pass, and each assertion is strong.

Findings:

`[]`

The tests are genuinely solid — I could not find a false-green. Every concern named in the brief is properly pinned:

- 60×k core (test c, line 134): pins `{ base: 180, weakness: null, dealt: 180 }` and `damage === 180`, plus `not.toContain("ATTACK_EFFECT_SKIPPED")` — not "damage > 0".
- Decline→0 (test d, lines 153-155): asserts NO `ENERGY_DISCARDED`, NO `DAMAGE_DEALT`, and `damage === 0` — proves both no damage and no 60× base leak, not just turn end. (A leaked base would emit `DAMAGE_DEALT`/60 and fail; in test c a leak would give 240 ≠ 180 and fail.)
- Weakness (test f, lines 208-213): pins `{ base: 120, weakness: { op: "multiply", amount: 2 }, dealt: 240 }` and `damage === 240` — the multiply modifier and the exact 240, not a coincidence.
- 2-Prize KO (test g, lines 234, 241): pins `phase.count === 2` AND `prizes.length === prizesBefore - 2`.

Fixtures verified correct:
- `fix-water-weak`: `weaknesses: [{ type: "Water", value: "×2" }]`, HP 300 (survives the doubled hit so the counter is readable).
- `fix-ko-ex`: name "Fixmon ex" (real " ex" suffix → `prizeValueOf` 2), HP 110, no weakness → 60×2=120 KOs with a real 10-HP margin.
- `fix-water-energy` provides {W}, `fix-energy` provides Colorless (non-{W}) — the exclusion assertion in test (b) is non-vacuous and empirically confirmed (discardable == the 2 waters only).
- `HAIL_BLADE_DECK` is 60 cards, 45 Basics / 15 Energy, so effectively mulligan-free; and the board is fully surgically determined (`setActiveFromDeck`/`attachFromDeck` pull from deck, actives pinned to `fix-hail-wall`), so opening-hand variance for seeds 1,3,5,7,8,9,10 cannot make a test pass for the wrong reason.

On the specific worries:
- `deriveAttackEffect(HAIL_BLADE_TEXT).toBeNull()` (test a, line 80): the text matches the fixture verbatim (line 316) and the registry comment; the deriver genuinely has no variable-count pattern so null is the intended refuse. It's self-checking (a wrong text that accidentally matched a pattern would make this FAIL, not silently pass), and the registry program overrides the deriver for tests b-g anyway, so it hides no bug. Not worth flagging.
- `programFor(id)?.attack` for the four ids: all four (sv02-061/236/261/274) map to `CHIEN_PAO` which has `attack: [...]`; `undefined?.attack` would fail `toBeDefined`, so the assertion is meaningful.
- No assertion reads a non-existent field that a loose matcher would swallow: `toMatchObject` requires the named keys present (missing `actor`/`weakness` would fail), `weakness: null` vs an absent field fails under Jest equality, and every `find(...)` result feeds `toMatchObject`/`toEqual` which fail on `undefined`.

Mutation-style cross-check: a wrong count, additive-instead-of-multiply weakness, a leaked 60× base, an active-instead-of-bench discard, an active-only (non-whole-board) scan, an offered non-{W}, or a 1-Prize ex value would each fail at least one of tests b/c/d/e/f/g.

- `damageDefender` damages the right victim (defender via `snipeActive` → `otherSeat`), reads the right slot (`discarded`), and yields 0 damage on empty pick / whiff (`recordMoved(record, op.recordAs, [])` on both the empty-board and empty-pick paths; `amount <= 0` guard).

- `attack.ts` `programDamage` only fires when a `damageDefender` op is present, so base-suppression and modifier-simulation never leak to other program attacks; the working-tree `program?.some(...) ?? false` refactor is behavior-identical.
- `effects.ts` derivers (`deriveAttackEffect` / `deriveAttackDamageBonus` / `deriveAttackDamageMultiplier`) all refuse the "any amount"/"for each card you discarded" text (anchored `^This attack does … Prize card …` regexes never match), so no double-scaling or crash.

The one real bug is at the **redaction/wire boundary**, caused directly by the new `upTo` arm — and `index.ts`'s changelog wrongly asserts "No web/API/DB/schema change."

```json
  {
    "file": "packages/engine/src/redact.ts",
    "line": 307,
    "summary": "redactedScopeOf silently collapses the new {kind:\"upTo\"} DiscardScope to {kind:\"each\"} because the ternary only special-cases \"total\", and the `satisfies DiscardScope` guard checks the RETURNED value, not input exhaustiveness — so it does NOT catch the missing arm (contrary to its own comment). The wire schema (redactedDiscardScopeSchema, packages/schema/src/match/redacted.ts:297) has no upTo member either.",
    "failure_scenario": "In an online match P1 attacks with Chien-Pao ex \"Hail Blade\"; the engine parks with scope {kind:\"upTo\", max:N}. The redactor sends {kind:\"each\"} to the client. The online discard dialog then treats it as the mandatory one-per-Pokémon \"each\" scope: the player can no longer DECLINE (empty pick), and if all N {W} sit on a single Pokémon the dialog forces exactly one discard — so online the card can only ever deal 60 (or 0), never 60×2/60×3. The server's validateChoice uses the real upTo scope, so whatever the crippled client sends is accepted, masking the divergence."
  },
  {
    "file": "src/features/online/components/OnlineHud.tsx",
    "line": 695,
    "summary": "The online discard dialog has no upTo branch: `required = scope.kind === \"total\" ? scope.count : groups.length` and `ready = picked.length === required` treat every non-total scope as a mandatory one-per-Pokémon \"each\", with no declinable/upTo path (its `scope` type, RedactedDiscardScope, cannot even represent upTo).",
    "failure_scenario": "Even after fixing redact.ts + the wire schema + projection.ts to carry upTo through, the online client would still force exactly `groups.length` picks and disallow the empty decline for Hail Blade, so online play stays broken. (Currently this defect is masked because redact.ts already collapses upTo→each upstream — but it is a second, independent fix the feature needs. GameHud.tsx got the upTo branch; OnlineHud.tsx did not.)"
  }
]
```

=== decisions.md D96 row context (135-138) ===
| D92 | Choice Belt — a TARGET-gated passive damage bonus, and the rule-box suffix read off the NAME (P3-M5, engine 0.43.0) | The `conditionalDamageBonus` row's **second and last card, closing it 2/2** — the target-gated twin of Vitality Band: "The attacks of the Pokémon this card is attached to do 30 more damage to your opponent's Active Pokémon **V** (before applying Weakness and Resistance)" (sv02-176). **Two calls carry it.** **(1) A SIBLING field, not the D40 vocabulary.** `PassiveEffects` gains **`damageBonusBeforeWRIfTarget: { amount, targetSuffix }`** beside D91's `damageBonusBeforeWRIf`, because the two gates ask different questions: D91's reads the ATTACKER's seat-relative board (a `BoardCondition`), this one reads the card being HIT. Folding it into the `BoardCondition` union would have meant inventing a condition whose subject is the defender — a different kind of predicate wearing the same name. The plumbing is D91's, unchanged in shape: the seat-free `passivesOf` collects these bonuses RAW into a new `targetConditionalDamageBonusBeforeWR` list (aggregation), and the FOLD stays in `interpreter.ts`'s `attackerPreWRBonus`, which now also takes the **`defenderCard`** — free, because both of the only two pre-W/R read sites already had it in hand (attack.ts's main hit had `defenderCard`, `snipeActive` had `target.card`), so **snipeActive parity is again free** and the module-cycle argument that put the fold in interpreter.ts still holds. **(2) The "is it a V" test needed NO schema, ingest, DB or API change.** tcgdex's dedicated `suffix` field is dropped at ingest — but the marker is ALSO part of the printed card NAME (a Pokémon V is literally printed "<Species> V"), and `name` IS persisted, so the datum survives *encoded in a column we already have*. A new **`cards.ts pokemonSuffixOf(card): "ex"|"V"|"VMAX"|"VSTAR"|"GX"|null`** derives it, matching each suffix as a WHOLE marker: "V" does not match "VMAX"/"VSTAR" (neither is a space-then-"V"), which is exactly the distinction the card draws — Choice Belt boosts a V, never a VMAX. The alternative (an ingest change + a migration + a backfill to persist `suffix`) would have been a multi-layer slice to recover a datum already in hand. It is a derivation, not a guess: the suffix is part of the printed name by the game's own naming rule. **Known and accepted: the gate is DORMANT against the live catalog.** The ingested SV-era pool contains no Pokémon V at all, so today Choice Belt is registered, correct, and never fires in a real game; it starts firing the moment a prior-era set is ingested, with no engine change. (1) **`packages/engine/src/hailBlade.test.ts`** now pins the attack behaviourally — **8 tests** covering the resume point's (a)–(g) plus a purity check: registry-authored (`programFor(sv02-061/236/261/274)?.attack` defined AND `deriveAttackEffect(verbatim)===null`); the DECLINABLE `{kind:"upTo",max:N}` park offering every {W} on the attacker's WHOLE board (Active+Bench) and NEVER a non-{W}; discard k → **60×k** to the defender with `ENERGY_DISCARDED{seat:p1,actor:p1}` + energy in P1's discard + NO `ATTACK_EFFECT_SKIPPED`; DECLINE (`uids:[]`) → **0 damage** (the "60× base suppressed" proof); a BENCHED Chien-Pao's {W} counts (whole-board reach); Weakness **DOUBLES** (60×2×2=240, `weakness:{op:"multiply",amount:2}`); an ex-defender KO takes **2 Prizes** (D93). A test-quality reviewer confirmed every assertion pins the specific number (no false-greens). No impl change was needed to make them pass — the #80 engine logic was correct.
(2) **Lint fix (`attack.ts:240`).** The `programDamage` line tripped biome `useOptionalChain` (`program !== null && program.some(...)` → `program?.some(...) ?? false`, behaviour-identical, still a strict `boolean`). Session #80 ran only `typecheck`, so this error had never surfaced; `bun run check` now goes green (**139 files / 1972 tests**, was 138/1964: +1 file, +8 tests).
(3) **`/code-review` (the review #80 never got).** Two independent finders converged on a REAL, CONFIRMED regression — **the online (P4) wire path was never updated for the new `{kind:"upTo",max}` `DiscardScope` arm.** `redact.ts:305` `redactedScopeOf`'s `satisfies DiscardScope` checks the RETURNED value (both `each`/`total` are valid), NOT input exhaustiveness — its own comment ("a new arm is a compile error") is STALE — so an `upTo` scope silently collapses into the `{kind:"each"}` else-branch. The wire schema (`packages/schema/src/match/redacted.ts:297` `redactedDiscardScopeSchema`), the client projection (`src/features/game/projection.ts:529`), and the online dialog (`src/features/online/components/OnlineHud.tsx:695`) ALL lack an `upTo` arm too. Net effect: **online Hail Blade is corrupted to a mandatory one-{W}-per-Pokémon "each" prompt — the player cannot decline (0/0 is impossible) and cannot discard 2+ off one Pokémon**, so online damage locks to (#Water-Pokémon × 60) with no choice; the engine's real `validateChoice` accepts whatever the crippled client sends, so it fails SILENTLY. LOCAL play (`GameHud.tsx` got the upTo branch in #80) is correct. The 937 engine tests bypass redaction/projection, so nothing caught it. **Deferred, not fixed** — a 4-file cross-package fix (engine + schema + client × 2) + an online-path test is its own coherent slice, and this iteration's budget/last-iteration status made a rushed cross-package change the wrong call. Logged as **D97** + on the backlog. `bun run check` GREEN. No web/API/DB/schema touch THIS session (tests + a one-line engine lint fix only). See D96 (impl), D97 (the review finding).
**NEXT (resume point):** **Plumb the new `{kind:"upTo",max}` `DiscardScope` through the ONLINE wire path** (D97 — a CONFIRMED P4 correctness bug found by this session's `/code-review`; local play is fine, online Hail Blade is broken). Four edits, all located:
(1) **`packages/schema/src/match/redacted.ts:297`** — add `z.object({ kind: z.literal("upTo"), max: z.number() })` to `redactedDiscardScopeSchema`'s discriminated union (so `RedactedDiscardScope` can CARRY the arm — this is the root cause that let the drop typecheck).
(2) **`packages/engine/src/redact.ts:305`** — `redactedScopeOf`: add the `scope.kind === "upTo"` case (`{ kind: "upTo", max: scope.max }`); and FIX the stale comment — note that `satisfies DiscardScope` on the OUTPUT does NOT enforce input exhaustiveness (a `switch` with `satisfies never` default, or mapping through `RedactedDiscardScope`, would).
(3) **`src/features/game/projection.ts:529`** — the client-side scope mapper (currently total→total / else→each) needs the `upTo` arm too, or it re-downgrades on the client.
(4) **`src/features/online/components/OnlineHud.tsx:695`** — the online `DiscardEnergyDialog` has no upTo branch (`required = scope.kind === "total" ? scope.count : groups.length`, `ready = picked.length === required`); mirror `GameHud.tsx`'s local upTo branch (capped multi-select, always-ready Confirm, empty decline allowed). Model on how GameHud reads the (now-carried) `upTo` scope.
Then **add an online-path test** that the redaction round-trips `upTo` (the layer the 937 engine tests bypass) — look for an existing redact/projection test to mirror, or a match-DO integration test. `bun run check` green. **AFTER that**, the P3-M5 backlog continues (`coverage-backlog.md`): the dormant **"count-2"** snipe (D94 warning: no verifiable real card) or a FRESH op-family row (`onDamagedByAttack`, `stadiumActivatedAbility`, `disableAbilities`, `damageAttacker`). USER-gated items (uploaded avatars, remote P4 deploy — migrations 0004+0005) still need the user. See D97.

### Prior header (P4 3c-viii — half-open socket liveness, kept for continuity)
**Last updated (was):** 2026-07-26 — build session #63 (**P4 3c-viii — half-open socket liveness**). The gap
3c-v's browser run surfaced, and the last known way an online match could stall. `setWebSocketAutoResponse`
answers the client's 1.5s ping WITHOUT waking the DO — the thing that makes hibernation worth having — but it
also means the DO can never notice pings that **stop**. A network that dies without a TCP close therefore
left a socket that looked perfectly live forever: `hasSocket` said yes, no disconnect grace was armed, no
forfeit clock started, and the opponent waited indefinitely. Every ORDINARY exit (tab close, browser kill,
navigation, reload, crash) delivers a close event, which is why this never bit in practice and why it took a
deliberate `set offline` to reproduce. **The fix reads the signal the runtime was already recording:**
`state.getWebSocketAutoResponseTimestamp(ws)` returns when it last auto-answered that socket, so liveness
costs nothing at ping time. The alternative — dropping the auto-response and stamping `lastSeen` in
`webSocketMessage` — was rejected on exactly that ground: ~40 wakes a minute per socket, hibernation given
up, to learn what the runtime already knows. **What it costs instead is a POLL,** because a quiet in-game
lobby schedules no alarm at all: `scheduleMaintenance` now pushes a **`LIVENESS_SWEEP_MS`** (30s) deadline
whenever any socket is connected, so an occupied lobby wakes twice a minute. **`SOCKET_SILENCE_MS`** is 15s —
ten missed pings, so a phone changing networks or a throttled background tab is not mistaken for a dead one —
and a test pins the budget that matters: sweep + silence + the 5s grace all fit inside the 90s forfeit, so a
dead network can never resolve SLOWER than a closed tab. A `null` timestamp counts as **ALIVE**, deliberately:
it is the state of every connection before its first ping, and nothing can distinguish "just opened" from
"opened long ago and never pinged". **The sweep only CLOSES** — the grace, the seat going disconnected and
the forfeit are all machinery a real close already drives, reached through the same `socketGone` (called
explicitly, since a server-side `close()` delivers no `webSocketClose` event to us). engine RULES UNCHANGED
(0.41.0); 1874 → **1878** tests. `bun run check` green. Built solo with full context; **self-reviewed, no
independent reviewer this session**. **BROWSER-VERIFIED with the very reproducer that exposed the bug:** with
a match live, one client was put offline with its socket left OPEN — before this change that produced nothing
at all, and now the opponent saw "disconnected — forfeits in 1:30" after ~50s (15s silence + up to 30s sweep
+ the 5s grace) with the countdown running. Bringing the client back online restored it within ~10s (the
channel reconnected, re-helloed, the forfeit was cancelled), while the client that stayed connected
throughout was never swept. Zero page errors. **With this, P4 has no known defects and no planned work left.**

user's go-ahead and credentials), or P5 polish.

later takes a freed seat stops getting the seatless board. **Players are NOT told they are being watched** —

### Prior header (P4 3c-v — the forfeit deadline on the wire + the opponent's countdown, kept for continuity)
**Last updated (was):** 2026-07-26 — build session #59 (**P4 3c-v — the forfeit deadline on the WIRE, and the
opponent's countdown**). The last silent path in the match lifecycle. 3c-ii could forfeit an abandoned player
and 3c-iv made a graceful leave do it instantly, but an UNGRACEFUL drop (a crash, a killed tab, a dead
network) still waited in total silence: the player who was still there watched a motionless board for 90
seconds and was then handed a win with no account of what had been decided. **The decision is WHERE the
deadline lives.** It moved out of the DO's private `ABANDON_KEY` storage list and onto
**`PlayerState.forfeitAt`** — a `@luminous/schema` WIRE type — so the number the opponent's countdown renders
is literally the number the alarm fires on, and the two cannot drift. The snapshot beat the `match` frame as
the carrier for three converging reasons: the arming moment (a disconnect grace expiring in `alarm()`) already
commits a snapshot and sends no match frame; a forfeit is lobby/transport state the engine knows nothing
about; and a reconnecting client gets it for free with the state it already receives. Mirroring it while
`ABANDON_KEY` stayed authoritative was rejected outright — two sources for one deadline is exactly how a
countdown ends up promising something the server won't do. **The invariant that makes it safe is `connected`
⇒ `forfeitAt === null`**, and it is enforced STRUCTURALLY: `setSeatConnected` takes the deadline as a final
argument defaulting to null (so you cannot write one without deciding the other), and
`seatGuest`/`reseatHost`/`makePlayer` clear it. That REPLACES 3c-ii's `clearDisconnectTimers`, whose entire
reason for existing was the fear that a future branch would cancel one timer and leave the other armed:
"mark them present" and "don't forfeit them" are now a single indivisible write instead of two calls.
`forfeitAbandoned` dissolved into the alarm, which judges due deadlines on the FINAL snapshot and consumes
them in the same commit. **A second, quieter piece: `readSnapshot`.** `SNAPSHOT_KEY` has no version gate, so
adding a field would have made every in-flight lobby unreadable across the deploy; it is now read through a
normalizer that fills fields added since the write — deliberately the OPPOSITE of D72's `MatchRecord` answer,
because a lobby snapshot is a handful of scalars with no embedded engine state (a missing field has exactly
one sensible value, and being wrong is cosmetic), and the guard is on the field's TYPE, not on nullishness,
because it feeds `Math.min` in the alarm scheduler where an `undefined` would set NaN. **Client:** a
top-centre `OpponentAwayBanner` — "Opp disconnected — forfeits in 1:30", ticking; "forfeiting…" past zero
rather than a frozen 0:00 (the server's alarm is what ends it and may lag the client clock); "waiting for
them to reconnect…" when no clock is armed; hidden once the game is over. engine RULES UNCHANGED (0.41.0);

reviewer this session** (offered — `/code-review` is user-triggered). **BROWSER-VERIFIED on two real clients,

notices. Every ordinary exit — tab close, browser kill, navigation, reload, crash — does produce a close
event, which is why this has never bitten.) Closing it needs server-side liveness and is its own slice.

### Prior resume point (P3-M5 Iono, kept for continuity)
**Iono is live (P3-M5, D39) — the hand-refresh Supporter family is CLOSED.** The
format's highest-play-rate Supporter needed **no new op**: three composable riders on
the D38 `handRefresh` op. **`toBottom?: true`** — the PLACEMENT: shuffle the **hand
alone** and append it UNDER the deck (`[...deck, ...shuffle(hand)]`) instead of
shuffling it into the deck, so the deck's existing order — and therefore the very next
draws — SURVIVE (the whole strategic point of Iono over Judge; pinned by a test
asserting the drawn cards are EXACTLY the pre-play deck top, in order).
**`draw:{kind:"prizeCount"}`** — each affected player draws their OWN remaining Prize
count (the player behind draws more); a Prize count is public, so the draw size leaks
nothing. **`onlyIfAnyMoved?: true`** — the draw clause fires only if ≥1 affected player
actually moved ≥1 card: an **all-or-nothing gate ACROSS the seats** ("if EITHER
player…"), not per-seat. That gate forced the op's one structural change: **two passes**
over the affected seats (all placements, then all draws) instead of D38's interleaved
move-then-draw — **behaviour-preserving** for Youngster/Judge/Brassius/Katy (per-seat
disjoint zones + `drawToHand` consumes NO rng ⇒ byte-identical states and rng threading,

+Session #80 landed the "Hail Blade" IMPLEMENTATION under a hard autoloop landing — typecheck-green but with NO dedicated tests and (it turns out) never `bun run check`'d. This session closed all three:

+(1) **`packages/engine/src/hailBlade.test.ts`** now pins the attack behaviourally — **8 tests** covering the resume point's (a)–(g) plus a purity check: registry-authored (`programFor(sv02-061/236/261/274)?.attack` defined AND `deriveAttackEffect(verbatim)===null`); the DECLINABLE `{kind:"upTo",max:N}` park offering every {W} on the attacker's WHOLE board (Active+Bench) and NEVER a non-{W}; discard k → **60×k** to the defender with `ENERGY_DISCARDED{seat:p1,actor:p1}` + energy in P1's discard + NO `ATTACK_EFFECT_SKIPPED`; DECLINE (`uids:[]`) → **0 damage** (the "60× base suppressed" proof); a BENCHED Chien-Pao's {W} counts (whole-board reach); Weakness **DOUBLES** (60×2×2=240, `weakness:{op:"multiply",amount:2}`); an ex-defender KO takes **2 Prizes** (D93). New fixtures in `testFixtures.ts` (byte-identical existing fixtures): `fix-hail-wall` (300 HP wall), `fix-water-weak` (×2 Water), `fix-ko-ex` (110 HP "Fixmon ex"), + a mulligan-free `HAIL_BLADE_DECK`. A test-quality reviewer confirmed every assertion pins the specific number (no false-greens). No impl change was needed to make them pass — the #80 engine logic was correct.

+(2) **Lint fix (`attack.ts:240`).** The `programDamage` line tripped biome `useOptionalChain` (`program !== null && program.some(...)` → `program?.some(...) ?? false`, behaviour-identical, still a strict `boolean`). Session #80 ran only `typecheck`, so this error had never surfaced; `bun run check` now goes green (**139 files / 1972 tests**, was 138/1964: +1 file, +8 tests).

+(3) **`/code-review` (the review #80 never got).** Two independent finders converged on a REAL, CONFIRMED regression — **the online (P4) wire path was never updated for the new `{kind:"upTo",max}` `DiscardScope` arm.** `redact.ts:305` `redactedScopeOf`'s `satisfies DiscardScope` checks the RETURNED value (both `each`/`total` are valid), NOT input exhaustiveness — its own comment ("a new arm is a compile error") is STALE — so an `upTo` scope silently collapses into the `{kind:"each"}` else-branch. The wire schema (`packages/schema/src/match/redacted.ts:297` `redactedDiscardScopeSchema`), the client projection (`src/features/game/projection.ts:529`), and the online dialog (`src/features/online/components/OnlineHud.tsx:695`) ALL lack an `upTo` arm too. Net effect: **online Hail Blade is corrupted to a mandatory one-{W}-per-Pokémon "each" prompt — the player cannot decline (0/0 is impossible) and cannot discard 2+ off one Pokémon**, so online damage locks to (#Water-Pokémon × 60) with no choice; the engine's real `validateChoice` accepts whatever the crippled client sends, so it fails SILENTLY. LOCAL play (`GameHud.tsx` got the upTo branch in #80) is correct. The 937 engine tests bypass redaction/projection, so nothing caught it. **Deferred, not fixed** — a 4-file cross-package fix (engine + schema + client × 2) + an online-path test is its own coherent slice, and this iteration's budget/last-iteration status made a rushed cross-package change the wrong call. Logged as **D97** + on the backlog. `bun run check` GREEN. No web/API/DB/schema touch THIS session (tests + a one-line engine lint fix only). See D96 (impl), D97 (the review finding).

+**NEXT (resume point):** **Plumb the new `{kind:"upTo",max}` `DiscardScope` through the ONLINE wire path** (D97 — a CONFIRMED P4 correctness bug found by this session's `/code-review`; local play is fine, online Hail Blade is broken). Four edits, all located:

+(1) **`packages/schema/src/match/redacted.ts:297`** — add `z.object({ kind: z.literal("upTo"), max: z.number() })` to `redactedDiscardScopeSchema`'s discriminated union (so `RedactedDiscardScope` can CARRY the arm — this is the root cause that let the drop typecheck).

+(2) **`packages/engine/src/redact.ts:305`** — `redactedScopeOf`: add the `scope.kind === "upTo"` case (`{ kind: "upTo", max: scope.max }`); and FIX the stale comment — note that `satisfies DiscardScope` on the OUTPUT does NOT enforce input exhaustiveness (a `switch` with `satisfies never` default, or mapping through `RedactedDiscardScope`, would).
+(3) **`src/features/game/projection.ts:529`** — the client-side scope mapper (currently total→total / else→each) needs the `upTo` arm too, or it re-downgrades on the client.

A dedicated test-quality reviewer found NO false-greens. **No impl change was needed** — the #80 engine logic (interpreter `discardEnergy from:"yours"`/`count:"any"`/`recordAs`, `damageDefender`, attack.ts base-suppression, effects.ts deriver-refusal) is correct as written. (2) **A biome lint error the hard-landing hid.** #80 ran only `typecheck`, never `bun run check`, so `attack.ts:240`'s `program !== null && program.some(...)` (a `useOptionalChain` violation) had never been caught; fixed to `program?.some(...) ?? false` (behaviour-identical, still strict `boolean`). `bun run check` now green — **139 files / 1972 tests** (was 138/1964). **The lesson: `typecheck`-green is NOT `check`-green; a hard-landing that skips the full gate can leave a lint error that only the NEXT session's gate surfaces.** (3) **The review caught a real, CONFIRMED P4 regression #80's "no web/API/schema touch" claim MISSED.** The new `DiscardScope` arm `{kind:"upTo",max}` was added to the engine but never plumbed through the online redaction/wire path: `redact.ts:305` `redactedScopeOf` silently collapses `upTo` into its `{kind:"each"}` else-branch — and its `satisfies DiscardScope` guard checks the RETURNED value (both `each`/`total` valid), NOT input exhaustiveness, so the drop TYPECHECKS and the guard's own comment ("a new arm is a compile error rather than a silent drop") is STALE/WRONG. The root enabler: `redactedDiscardScopeSchema` (`packages/schema/src/match/redacted.ts:297`) has no `upTo` member, so `{kind:"each"}` is a valid `RedactedDiscardScope` and nothing forces the arm. `projection.ts:529` and `OnlineHud.tsx:695` likewise lack `upTo`. **Effect:** online Hail Blade renders as a MANDATORY one-{W}-per-Pokémon prompt — no decline, no 2+-off-one-Pokémon — so online damage locks to (#Water-Pokémon × 60); the engine's `validateChoice` accepts the crippled client's picks, so it fails SILENTLY. Since M9 the app runs on the real API, so this is the PRIMARY path; the 937 engine tests bypass redaction/projection entirely, so nothing caught it. Local play (`GameHud.tsx` got the upTo branch in #80) is correct. **Disposition: DEFERRED to its own slice, not fixed here.** A 4-file cross-package fix (schema + engine redact + client projection + online HUD) + an online round-trip test is a coherent slice on its own, and this iteration's remaining budget on a LAST autoloop iteration made a rushed cross-package change the wrong call — the autoloop design ("a fresh session with a good resume point beats a rushed one") applies exactly here. Recorded as the NEXT resume point with all four file:line targets + on `coverage-backlog.md`. *Why: the review earned its keep — a slice that self-reviewed as "no web/API touch" had, in fact, a silent online-only correctness bug that only a redaction-aware reader (not the engine test suite) could see; and writing the tests first meant the review ran against a KNOWN-good engine, isolating the finding to the wire layer.* (2026-07-27) |

# Decisions & Locked Assumptions

## Product / architecture decisions
| # | Decision | Choice |
|---|---|---|
| D1 | Backend data strategy | Own DB — ingest tcgdex → Cloudflare D1, serve our own API |
| D2 | Accounts & persistence | Full accounts + auth; users own their decks |
| D2a | Auth methods | Email + password **and** social OAuth (Discord + Google) |
| D3 | Catalog scope | Full-history-capable schema, ingest SV-era first |
| D4 | Card images | Mirror into R2, serve from our domain |
| D5 | Card type | Unify — one canonical `Card`; builder/playmat are view projections |
| D6 | Online lobby server | In scope — real Durable Object (WebSocket) lobby |
| D7 | Game engine placement | Separate **`packages/engine`** (pure logic) — imported by both `apps/web` (local play) and `apps/api` (authoritative DO). *Why: the engine runs in two runtimes; an app can't import another app.* |
| D8 | Card-effect modeling | **Composable, data-driven op programs** over shared archetype templates (not per-card functions); engine emits **semantic events** consumed by the animation layer. *Why: cards are minor variations on a few archetypes; keeps authoring + animation cheap. Detail in `workstreams/simulator.md`.* |
| D9 | Image mirroring & ingest execution (refines D4/§3.4) | Images mirror into R2 **lazily** — a Worker route (`GET /assets/…`) serves from R2 and on miss fetches tcgdex origin, stores, streams; catalog rows keep tcgdex **origin** URLs. Card-data backfill runs as a **local Bun script** applying batched upsert SQL via `wrangler d1 execute`; a future cron does small in-Worker deltas only. *Why: a full SV backfill is ~10k images — over Worker subrequest limits in one shot and hours of CLI puts; cache-aside mirrors exactly what's viewed and stays within limits.* (2026-07-09) |
| D10 | M9 catalog search shape (refines D5/§6) | `CardBrief` **extended** with `types/hp/regulationMark/stage/trainerType/energyType` (card-table columns only — **no set join**, so no `setName`); `GET /cards` gains **repeatable `type`/`rarity`** (OR within a dimension) and **`sort=name\|hp-desc\|set`**; KV cache keys version-prefixed (`catalog:v2:`) so a shape change can't serve stale briefs. The builder consumes briefs through one adapter (`src/features/builder/catalog.ts` — accented `"Pokémon"`, stage/trainerType/energyType → the single `subtype`). *Why: the grid/filters/deck-math need those fields per tile; per-tile full-Card fetches or a fixture pool were the alternatives.* (2026-07-13) |
| D11 | M9 scope trims (pending P2) | **Kinds** (`subtypes`) filter stays a client-side per-page heuristic (server can't express OR across stage/trainerType; EX/Mega are name-regexes until structured data — P2 tasks 8-9). **Manual deck/folder reorder is session-only** (no position field in the schema — P2 task 17). **Folder delete keeps the lift-up UX client-side** (child PATCHes before DELETE) over the server's cascade semantics. **`RARITIES` is a hardcoded tcgdex vocabulary snapshot** in the rail. *Why: each would widen M9's already-large surface; all four are logged with their fixes in `workstreams/deck-builder.md`.* (2026-07-13) **Revised 2026-07-14 (P2-M1):** kinds now filter **server-side** (repeatable `stage`/`trainerType`/`energyType`) — only EX/Mega remain a client-side name-regex post-filter (tcgdex `suffix` not persisted; follow-up logged); hardcoded vocabularies replaced by **`GET /facets`**. Reorder (task 17) and lift-up remain as decided. **Revised again 2026-07-14 (task 17):** reorder is now persisted — see D13; only the lift-up trim still stands. |
| D12 | P2-M1 catalog surface & legality source of truth | `GET /cards` gains **repeatable `id`** (≤100, deck hydration in ONE call; chunked IN + in-memory ordering twin of the SQL sort), **`nameExact`** (case-insensitive whole-name equality), `serie`, `illustrator`, `text` (LIKE over ability/attack JSON), plus the kind params above; **`GET /facets`** serves the filter vocabularies (7 DISTINCTs, one db.batch, KV-cached). `CardBrief` += **`legal {standard,expanded}`**; KV namespace → **`catalog:v3:`**, with KV **bypassed** for >512-byte keys and any `?id=` request (per-deck id sets never recur — caching them is pure write waste). Web: **`Format.legalFlag`** keys BOTH the `legalOnly` filter (`legal=<flag>`) and `isLegalInFormat` (structured verdict beats printed mark; mark check only for legal-less fixtures) — one legality definition for grid + validator. Deck rules: **Radiant = 1 per deck total** (like ACE SPEC; official rule), Prism Star = 1 per name. *Why: filters needed server truth for correct totals; hydration was an N-request fan-out; legality had two disagreeing definitions.* (2026-07-14) |
| D13 | Manual-order persistence model (P2 task 17) | `position` INTEGER on `decks` and `folders` — **global per user, not per folder**: the web grid's flat array (position-ascending) IS the manual order, per-view filtering preserves relative order, and a nest move keeps the row's slot (folderId changes, position doesn't) — exactly the client's existing semantics. Creates take **min−1** (new rows prepend); migration 0003 backfills existing rows in the old name-order so nothing visibly moves. A reorder permutes the in-view rows **among their own slots' position values** (`applyReorder` returns the rewritten array + the changed `{id, position}` pairs) and persists via **`POST /decks/reorder` / `/folders/reorder`** — absolute assignments, ≤500 rows, applied atomically in one db.batch; unknown/foreign ids → 400 naming them; failure recovery is **resync**, not per-row rollback (the folder-delete precedent). Reorder deliberately does NOT bump `updated`. *Why: slot-permutation keeps payloads at the size of the move (not the scope), needs no renumbering pass ever, and one atomic endpoint beats N racing PATCHes.* (2026-07-14) |

| D14 | Engine core contract (P3-M1) | **`applyAction(state, action) → {ok:true, state, events} | {ok:false, error}`** — one reducer, never throws, never mutates. `GameState` is plain JSON (the mulberry32 `rngState` lives **inside** it, so same seed + same actions replay identically); card instances are **uids** (`"p1#0"`) over an injected `cardPool` carried in the state (keeps `applyAction` a pure 2-arg pair and snapshots self-contained). Seats **`p1`/`p2` are labels, not turn order** — the coin winner *chooses* first via an action, `firstPlayer` records it. **Choices are actions; mandatory steps auto-resolve** inside the reducer (mulligan redraws, prize setting, the turn-start draw), so a `Phase` exists only where a player owes a decision. **Events are the animation + wire contract** (semantic, serializable, payloads always copied — never aliasing state or the caller's action). **Wire-safety:** TS types are not input validation — P4 decodes actions from clients, so every index/seat/count an action carries is runtime-checked (three real card-destroying bugs came from exactly this: a JSON string `"1"` bench index). *Why: the engine runs in two runtimes (web local play + the authoritative DO), and an authoritative server needs a total, replayable, non-throwing function of (state, action).* (2026-07-14) |
| D15 | Mulligan compensation (rules correction) | Each player may draw 1 card **per opponent mulligan**, and **mulliganing yourself does not forfeit it** — so **both** seats can be owed at once (each off the other's count). `reference/ptcg-rules.md` §3.5 previously read "the non-mulliganing player", which the M1 engine implemented as an exemption that does not exist; the reference doc is corrected and the phase now carries a per-seat `owed`/`decided` map. The compensation draw is **clamped** so a player can never draw below the 6 cards they must still set aside as prizes. *Why: a wrong rule in the spec propagated straight into the engine — the reference doc is the source of truth and had to be fixed at the source.* (2026-07-14) |
| D16 | M2 staged turn tail, KO interrupts & damage modifiers (P3-M2) | The turn tail is a **`pending: PendingStage[]` queue** on `GameState`, drained by `advance()` (flow.ts): automatic stages run, decision stages either **park** (phase becomes the matching `ko:takePrizes`/`ko:promote` interrupt, prompt event emitted) or **auto-resolve** when only one legal resolution exists. `attack` seeds `takePrizes`+`promote` ahead of the shared `turnTail(seat)` triple. The parked phase mirrors `pending[0]` (dual encoding, kept deliberately for M2): handlers cross-check the two and reject with **`PHASE_DESYNC`** on mismatch. Win evaluation lives in ONE place — the shared `resolvePrizesAndResume`/`resolvePromotionAndResume` helpers used by both the action handlers and advance's auto-resolves. `gameOver` carries **`GameOutcome`** (`win {winner, reason}` \| `tie {reasons}`); sudden death is surfaced as `tie`, not played out. Printed weakness/resistance parse to a **`DamageModifier {op: multiply\|add\|subtract, amount}`** (×N / +N / −N; unknown garble keeps modern-era ×2/−30 defaults) applied weakness→resistance, floor 0 (§8.5); `DAMAGE_DEALT` carries the modifiers so animators can show the math. Data gaps never guess a KO: `hp ≤ 0` reads as the null data gap. *Why: KO resolution must pause mid-tail for player choices, M3's checkup KOs reuse the same interrupts, and additive legacy weakness ("+20", schema-documented) was being silently misread as ×2.* (2026-07-16) |
| D17 | Engine→playmat projection contract (P3) | **`projectGameState(state, viewerSeat) → GameProjection`** (`src/features/game/projection.ts`): `{ board, piles, pokemon, turn, activePlayer, waitingOn, pendingDecision, outcome }` — `board` is a drop-in playmat `BoardState` (`you` = viewer); the wrapper carries what BoardState can't (`piles` deckCount/discard, `pokemon` = per-uid `{damage, hp}`, `outcome` per-viewer win/tie). **`activePlayer` = turn owner; `waitingOn` = the seat that must act NOW** — the split exists because during `ko:promote` the actor is the NON-turn player (the KO'd defender), and a UI gating on turn ownership alone soft-locks. Hidden info is redacted structurally: opponent hand = positional backs (`opponent-hand-N`, no uids — a uid is stable across zones and would let a client track a hidden card), both prize piles = counts only, decks = counts. Public cards key off the engine **uid** so the Pixi layer animates a card as one object across projections. The phase mapping is an **exhaustive switch** (`satisfies never`) — a new engine phase is a compile error, not a silent guess. *Why: this is the same per-viewer filter P4's server will apply; building it client-side first pins the contract with tests.* (2026-07-16) **Revised 2026-07-17 (wire-up review):** during any `setup:*` phase the OPPONENT's active/bench also project as face-down backs (positional `-hidden` ids, no `pokemon` rows — a row would leak the uid key + printed HP); a hot-seat viewer flip at Ready was exposing the first player's face-down placements. Reveal re-keys positional→uid (remount, not flip) — the same trade as hand backs. |

| D18 | Local play page & engine card-pool sourcing (P3 wire-up) | **`/play`** is a hot-seat local match: `GamePage` owns `GameState` via `useLocalGame` (pure reducer over `applyAction`), renders `projectGameState` through the extracted presentational **`PlaymatView`** (the `/simulator` mock, retitled "Sandbox", is a thin wrapper driver), and the **viewer follows `waitingOn`** for the device flip. The engine `cardPool` is built client-side by **fanning out `GET /cards/:id`** (`src/features/game/cardPool.ts`, concurrency 8, module-level promise cache; 404s cache as stable `missing`, rejections self-evict) — NOT via the brief-returning batch route. *Why: `CardBrief` deliberately omits the combat blobs (attacks/weakness/retreat) the engine reads; the per-id route already serves the full canonical Card KV-cached, and this needed no api change while api deploys stay user-gated. A `?full` batch param is the logged follow-up to bundle with the next deploy.* (2026-07-17) |
| D19 | Drop-legality is a driver-supplied predicate (P3 wire-up review) | `AnimatedCardsLayer` takes an optional **`PlacementPredicate`** (defaults to the sandbox's `canPlace`, so the mock is untouched); `/play` supplies `gamePlacementPredicate(game, viewerSeat)` — a deliberately **coarse, gesture-class** gate (phase-aware: what CAN ever map to an action) kept in lockstep with `moveToAction` by a property test (every afforded drop translates to a non-null action). Fine-grained legality stays with `applyAction` + the error pill. Hand→hand reorder is rejected on /play (the engine owns hand order; affording it was a silent lie). *Why: the phase-unaware mock `canPlace` afforded gestures the engine could never accept (accept-animation → wrong-rule error pill), and M4 evolve/trainer drags can't be expressed through it — the seam had to move to the driver.* (2026-07-17) |
| D20 | Text-derived attack effects (P3-M3) | Status-applying attacks resolve through a **conservative exact-sentence deriver** (`packages/engine/src/effects.ts`): five anchored whole-effect patterns ("Your opponent's Active Pokémon is now {X}.", the coin-flip-gated variant, "This Pokémon is now {X}.", the Rest heal compound, the raised-poison Checkup variant) compile to a tiny **`EffectStep[]`** program (applyStatus/heal/coinFlipGate) executed after damage, before the KO check; ANY other text keeps today's loud `ATTACK_EFFECT_SKIPPED`. This is the first sliver of D8's op-program system — M4's id-keyed registry will sit ABOVE it (`programFor(cardId) ?? derive(text)`), and the interpreter is deliberately still attack-private until M4's ops force its real shape. **Self-`Paralyzed` is excluded from the self-pattern**: official wording clears paralysis only if "Paralyzed since the beginning of your last turn", so self-paralysis at your own turn's end must SURVIVE the immediate checkup — our blanket ended-seat clear (correct for every opponent-inflicted case) would wrongly erase it, so the deriver refuses the sentence until paralysis carries an applied-turn stamp; `reference/ptcg-rules.md` §12/§13.4 corrected at the source (the D15 precedent). Demo decks swapped in real status attackers (Numel sv03-031 ×3 Fire/Burn, Luvdisc sv02-047 ×3 Water/Asleep) so /play exercises the pipeline. *Why: statuses without an application path are dead code until M4; exact-sentence matching makes dozens of real cards fully simulated with zero guessing, and the apostrophe class (`['’]`) is the only tolerance so a re-ingest can't silently un-derive them.* (2026-07-17) |
| D21 | Battle state rides the CardModel (P3-M3 surface) | `CardModel` gains **`battle?: {damage, hp, conditions}`**, attached by the projection to in-play Pokémon only — the `statuses` side-table (`GameProjection.pokemon`, prop-drilled 5 hops to DamageChip) is DELETED; chips (damage + the new SLP/PAR/CNF/BRN/PSN pills) read the card they decorate. The playmat stays engine-free: `BattleConditions` is a structural restatement of the engine's `SpecialConditions`, pinned by a **two-way compile-time assignability assert** in `battleStateOf` (an added engine condition field fails the build instead of silently never rendering); `conditions` is REQUIRED (`NO_CONDITIONS` const for mocks) so a missing object can't read as "no conditions" downstream. The checkup itself runs entirely inside `advance` — **no new Phase members**; its KOs park on the existing ko:* interrupts, and the projection reports **`activeSeat: null` for between-turns parks** (discriminated by the pending queue: an in-turn KO still carries its endTurn/checkup tail, a checkup KO has drained it to bare startTurn). *Why: the side-table was the wire-up review's known wart; co-location kills the drilling, and the vocabulary stays out of the playmat per the zero-engine-imports rule — lift it to `@luminous/schema` when M4 markers force the shape to grow.* (2026-07-17) |

| D23 | Trainers + Abilities via a resumable effect interpreter (P3-M4 slice 2) | The real first appearance of D8's op-program system (D20's deriver was "the first sliver"). **One shared interpreter** (`packages/engine/src/interpreter.ts`) runs every op program — attacks, Trainers, Abilities alike; the M3 attack-private `runEffectSteps` is GONE. Attacks resolve `programFor(id)?.attack ?? deriveAttackEffect(text)` at the one call site (registry ABOVE the deriver, `registry.ts`); Trainers/Abilities have NO text deriver — an unauthored one loudly can't be played/used rather than guessing. **Mid-effect decisions PARK** via a new `effect:choose` Phase carrying a JSON continuation (`{pendingOp, rest, ctx}`) — replayable, and OUTSIDE the KO/win tail (no in-scope effect KOs or ends the game, so the interpreter never touches flow.ts). A DONE program drains straight into the stage — identical to the old inline call, one hop later; a PARKED one leaves it in `pending` until `resolveEffect` finishes the program (across any number of re-parks) and drains it then. **`resumeTail` is REDEFINED, deliberately:** it meant "this program is mid-KO-sweep (an on-KO Ability)" and now means "this program is mid-TAIL — the stages that finish the job are already queued behind it, so DONE means keep draining, not fold back to a turn". Both callers want exactly that, and neither wants the mid-turn KO sweep. The one place they differ is the projection: an on-KO park has `phase.seat` ≠ the turn owner, an attack park has `phase.seat` = the turn owner — `koParkActiveSeat` resolves both off the pending queue, so `attackEpilogue` joined `endTurn`/`checkup`/`resumeTurn` as an in-turn marker. **The family that proves it is DERIVED, not authored:** `discardEnergy` gained a **`yourActive`** arm (the controller's own Active — for an attack, the printed "this Pokémon", §8) and a **`count: "all"`** rider, and two anchored whole-sentence deriver rules cover **12 catalog rows with ZERO registry rows** — "Discard an Energy from this Pokémon." (Houndoom sv01-034/sv03-133, Charcadet, Staraptor, Paldean Tauros, Dedenne ex ×2, Bombirdier) and "Discard all Energy from this Pokémon." (Pawmot ×2, Raichu ×2). Deliberately NOT derived: the numeric counts ("Discard 2/3 Energy" — needs an exact-N park) and the typed ones (Kilowattrel's "a {L} Energy" — needs an energy-of-type filter, and `{L}` means an Energy that PROVIDES {L}, so Special Energy counts). **Third idea, and the one the review sharpened most: INTERCHANGEABLE CANDIDATES COLLAPSE.** `interchangeableCandidates` keeps one representative per (host, energy identity) before the forced/park decision, so a Houndoom attacking with three {R} attached asks nothing — the M1 "a choice with no choice in it is not a choice" doctrine applied to card identity, via the `attachEnergyFrom` fungibility precedent. WHICH POKÉMON loses the Energy is never fungible, so the key includes the host. **The identity is NOT the catalog id** — the review caught that the real catalog prints Basic Fire Energy under three ids (sve-002/010/018), so an id key would have parked a real deck on a non-choice and broken the slice's own headline claim; a Basic keys on what it PROVIDES, everything else on its id (the two spaces prefixed apart, so a Basic {R} and a Special providing {R} never merge). | D80 | Half-open sockets are swept with the runtime's OWN keepalive timestamp (P4 online, increment 3c-viii) | The gap 3c-v's browser run surfaced, and the last known way an online match could stall. `setWebSocketAutoResponse` answers the client's 1.5s ping without waking the DO — the thing that makes hibernation worth having — but it also means the DO can never notice pings that STOP. A network that dies without a TCP close therefore left a socket that looked perfectly live forever: `hasSocket` said yes, no disconnect grace was armed, no forfeit clock started, and the opponent waited indefinitely. Every ORDINARY exit (tab close, browser kill, navigation, reload, crash) delivers a close event, which is why this never bit in practice and why it took a deliberate `set offline` to reproduce. **The fix is to read the signal the runtime was already recording:** `state.getWebSocketAutoResponseTimestamp(ws)` returns when it last auto-answered that socket, so liveness costs nothing at ping time. The alternative — dropping the auto-response and stamping `lastSeen` in `webSocketMessage` — was rejected on exactly that ground: it would wake the DO ~40 times a minute per socket and give up hibernation to learn what the runtime already knows. **What it costs instead is a POLL**, because a quiet in-game lobby schedules no alarm at all: `scheduleMaintenance` now pushes a `LIVENESS_SWEEP_MS` (30s) deadline whenever any socket is connected, so an occupied lobby wakes twice a minute. `SOCKET_SILENCE_MS` is 15s — ten missed pings, so a phone changing networks or a throttled background tab is not mistaken for a dead one — and a test pins the budget that matters: sweep + silence + the 5s grace all fit inside the 90s forfeit, so a dead network can never resolve slower than a closed tab. **A `null` timestamp counts as ALIVE**, deliberately: it is the state of every connection before its first ping, and nothing can distinguish "just opened" from "opened long ago and never pinged" — the cost of that reading is a socket we never sweep, versus closing a healthy one-second-old connection. **The sweep only CLOSES**; everything after it — the grace, the seat going disconnected, the forfeit — is the machinery a real close already drives, reached through the same `socketGone` (called explicitly, since a server-side `close()` delivers no `webSocketClose` event to us). 1874 → **1878** tests. **BROWSER-VERIFIED with the very reproducer that exposed the bug:** with a match live, one client was put offline with the socket left open; before this change that produced nothing at all, and now the opponent saw "disconnected — forfeits in 1:30" after ~50s (15s silence + up to 30s sweep + the 5s grace) and the countdown ran. Bringing the client back online restored it within ~10s — the channel reconnected, re-helloed, and the forfeit was cancelled — while the client that stayed connected throughout was never swept. Zero page errors. *Why: the cheapest signal is the one someone else is already recording. Hibernation exists to avoid waking on keepalives, so any fix that inspects keepalives directly is self-defeating; asking the runtime when it last answered turns a per-ping cost into a per-half-minute one.* (2026-07-26) |

# Simulator coverage — the new-op backlog (P3-M5)

The engine simulates cards as **data-driven op programs** (registry.ts). A card
is playable when its printed effect maps onto the op vocabulary
(`effects.ts` EffectOp, plus the continuous/energy/ability shapes in
`registry.ts`). M4 built the vocabulary through nine slices; M5 expands **card
coverage** across the SV-era pool.

## Method — a classify → verify Workflow fan-out (2026-07-19)
The 140 un-authored **sv01–sv03** Trainers (61), Special Energies (4) and
Pokémon Abilities (75) were classified by a 10-agent fan-out (5 batches ×
classify + adversarial verify), each card judged against the current op
vocabulary with the deriver doctrine — **exact map or flag** (a wrong-but-plausible
program is worse than a flag). Every authorable program was then hand-verified
against the local catalog before landing.

## Result
| Verdict | Count |
|---|---|
| **authorable now** (landed this pass) | **5** |
| needs a new op (backlog below) | 113 |
| already authored (M4) | 22 |
| **total classified** | 140 |

Only ~4% of the un-authored pool is expressible with today's ops — coverage is
**op-bound, not authoring-bound**: each new primitive unlocks a whole family, so
the backlog below (ranked by cards-unlocked) is the roadmap for the next slices.
Authoring is then a few registry rows per card, exactly as D8 intended.

### Authored this pass (M5 #1)
| Card | id | Program |
